chapter_title: Chương 293: Ngôi nhà mới của gia đình

segments.title: Chương 293: Ngôi nhà mới của gia đình
segments.content:
It was almost dusk when they entered the village.

Looking at the newly paved cement road, Yang Shuo couldn't help but exclaim, "Wow, this is really convenient now!"

The village road was even smoother than the county road.

After the local government had filled its coffers by selling land, it had allocated funds to repave the county road once. But after only a little over half a year, it was once again riddled with potholes from the weight of large trucks.

Dealing with the village road was simpler. They just built two width-restricting cement posts, allowing only three-wheelers, small cars, small trucks, and tractors to pass through.

Chen Guiliang rolled down his window and stuck his head out to observe the road, feeling a surge of pride. He had donated more than half the money for its construction.

"The scenery in your village is quite nice. It's all so green in the winter," Bian Guanyue was also observing, though she was looking at the distant mountains.

Chen Guiliang said, "More and more villagers are going out to work as migrant laborers, so more and more mountain land is being left fallow. And for the land by the river, it's mandatory to return farmland to forest. The state provides subsidies for planting trees and bamboo. That's why it's so green everywhere now."

Bian Guanyue leaned against the window, curiously watching the scenery along the way.

The car didn't stop at his maternal grandmother's house. Yang Shuo drove directly to the hollow opposite Chen Guiliang's home. He then helped take the New Year's goods out of the trunk and carried them with Chen Guiliang across the field ridges and over the mountain hollow.

"Bro!"

His cousin, Chen Guirong, was squatting outside their courtyard, setting off firecrackers with two little kids from the neighborhood.

The mustard greens there had already been harvested to be pickled, leaving behind rows of stalks, which they were blasting to bits with firecrackers.

Chen Guiliang shouted, "Come over and help with the things!"

His cousin immediately scampered over.

"This is your sister-in-law. Help her carry her suitcase," Chen Guiliang introduced. "This is my cousin, Chen Guirong."

"Happy New Year, Big Brother and Sister-in-law," Chen Guirong greeted as he took the suitcase.

Bian Guanyue quickly said, "There's no need, I can get it myself."

But Chen Guirong simply took hold of a corner of the suitcase.

On the uphill path of the hollow, there were some spots where you couldn't roll the suitcase and had to carry it.

Bian Guanyue couldn't win against his insistence and could only say, "Thank you."

"Don't mention it, it's nothing." Chen Guirong didn't just carry it, he intentionally hoisted it onto his shoulder to show off his strength.

Chen Guiliang asked, "I heard you dropped out of high school and went to a vocational school to study cooking?"

Chen Guirong said, "High school was boring. Our school was terrible, the teachers didn't really care, and the students were all just messing around. After I got into a fight, I was given a major demerit. Son of a... uh, with Sister-in-law here, I won't curse. The other guy clearly started it, and it was his fault too. The school just punished both sides equally. I was so mad I just quit. At least with cooking, I'll have a skill."

"Study hard, then go work in a restaurant for a few years," Chen Guiliang said. "Once you're familiar with the restaurant business, I'll put up the money for you to open one too. You'll hold the majority of the shares, just give me a cut of the profits."

Chen Guirong was overjoyed. "Then it's a deal. I might not be good at studying, but I've been a great cook since I was a kid."

As they spoke, they had already reached the top of the hollow.

There were two other families there, who greeted Chen Guiliang warmly as soon as they saw him.

In one of those families lived Chen Guiliang's childhood sweetheart. They often got "married" when playing house as kids. They had even promised to get married for real when they grew up and had already picked out many names for their children.

But before she even graduated from vocational high school, she became pregnant with a classmate's child. So she dropped out, held a wedding banquet, and went to get a marriage certificate once she was of age. Now, her child was already in kindergarten.

"Brother Guiliang!"

A kid who was about to graduate from junior high ran out of his house.

That was Zeng Xiaoming, the younger cousin of Chen Guiliang's childhood sweetheart. He came over on his own initiative to help Chen Guiliang carry the New Year's goods.

Chen Guiliang wished him a Happy New Year.

After crossing the hollow, he saw a brand-new, three-story Western-style house on the mountainside.

As he got closer, he could smell the aroma of cooking.

Knowing Chen Guiliang was coming home tonight, his parents and grandmother had already prepared a great feast and were waiting.

When Chen Guiliang arrived in his own courtyard, he immediately opened the suitcase filled with New Year's goods and handed Zeng Xiaoming a language repeater and two cassette tapes of songs.

"For me?" Zeng Xiaoming was incredulous.

Chen Guiliang smiled, "Take it. you can still use it in high school."

Language repeaters weren't worth much anymore; even brand-name ones only cost a hundred or so yuan. But to a village kid who had barely even been to the county town, it seemed exceptionally precious.

Chen Guiliang had bought New Year's gifts for the children of several nearby neighbors.

As for his cousin, he directly gave him a Nokia phone. It used to sell for several thousand, but the price had now dropped to just over six hundred.

"Bro, you're the man! I'll follow you from now on!" His cousin, Chen Guirong, was all smiles.

Chen Guiliang said, "You should just focus on learning to cook."

His parents and grandmother had come out of the house, taking the luggage from Chen Guiliang and Yang Shuo with beaming faces. At the same time, they all looked at Bian Guanyue, waiting for Chen Guiliang's introduction.

Chen Guiliang said, "Dad, Mom, Grandma, this is my girlfriend, Bian Guanyue."

"Hello, Grandma. Hello, Uncle and Auntie!" Bian Guanyue bowed gracefully.

His mother, Yao Lan, was grinning from ear to ear. "Good, good, good, hurry inside and take a seat."

Yang Shuo also greeted the elders, put down the luggage, and left.

He had to go home for the New Year too, and he was taking the borrowed car home with him. When Chen Guiliang needed it, he would drive back over to pick him up.

"Go wash your hands and eat. The food is getting cold," his grandmother reminded them.

The table was filled with a sumptuous spread of dishes. The sight made Chen Guiliang's mouth water; most of these dishes were impossible to find in the capital.

He was ravenous.

Damn it, when the company builds its own building in the future, I'll have to set up an employee cafeteria. I'll hire two chefs who cook Longdu cuisine, just to make special meals for me.

But some of the ingredients were hard to buy, which was also a problem.

The elders didn't serve Bian Guanyue food with their chopsticks; the family didn't have that tradition. But they eagerly introduced the dishes, encouraging her to try everything on the table.

They also didn't pry into what Bian Guanyue's family did. Chen Guiliang's family members weren't gossips. All that mattered was knowing that she was the girlfriend their son had brought home.

The house had been rebuilt, but the color TV hadn't been replaced. It was still the one Chen Guiliang had bought after his rebirth.

But they had bought a DVD player and speakers, so his dad could watch Hong Kong and Taiwanese martial arts films, and his grandmother could watch Sichuan opera discs.

As for his mom, she liked perming her hair and playing mahjong.

Before, she couldn't bear to spend money on perms and would even grow her hair long to cut and sell. She had no time to play mahjong either, busy with work all year round.

Now, her daily life consisted of happily going to town to get her hair permed, and she also liked dyeing it brown. She also wore clothes that she thought were very fashionable, but were actually long out of style.

At a glance, she looked like a fashionable woman from the coastal areas in the 1990s.

That was her first impression of fashion and glamour from when she had gone to work in Yangcheng, and she had always dreamed of being able to dress like that herself.

One could only say that she was a perfect match for his father, who rode a motorcycle wearing a floral shirt, beach shorts, and sunglasses.

His mom was a regular winner at mahjong, but even with her son being wealthy, she only played for 50 cents a game in the village. Her opponents were all veterans too, and in half a day, the most you could win or lose was twenty or thirty yuan.

Some villagers, however, were quite something else. They didn't earn much money, but they insisted on playing mahjong for 5 yuan a game. The wins and losses could easily be several hundred yuan at a time.

They chatted idly while eating.

Speaking of mahjong, his dad animatedly recounted the big news in the village.

"It just happened this month," Chen Xinhua said excitedly. "Every day, people drove to the village to play Golden Flower, carrying their money in boxes. They hired the idle men in the village, posting one person on each hill as a lookout. They paid a hundred yuan a day for lookout duty. A few days ago, someone reported them. The police raiding the gambling den went straight for the place they were playing cards. It scared them so much they threw their money into the river."

Chen Guiliang had heard about this in his past life, but he still played along for his dad's sake, "Where did all those rich people come from?"

Chen Xinhua said, "Some had a local accent, some had a Rongcheng accent, and some had a Jiucheng accent. I don't know what kind of business they're in, but they all drove nice cars."

"Did they get caught?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Chen Xinhua said, "They caught two in the mountains and four at a farmer's house. The rest supposedly turned themselves in. There's only one exit from the village, so their cars were blocked and couldn't get out. The police also had the villagers fish out the money they threw into the river. Another one fled to your Sixth Grandpa's house, stuffed the money under the bed, and said it was a gift for your Sixth Grandpa. Your Sixth Grandpa was afraid of trouble and turned it all over to the police."

A story so exciting would be enough for the villagers to talk about for years.
